newsitem.title: FRANCE: Netanyahu says tunnel riot based on disinformation.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says tunnel riot based on disinformation.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday that Palestinian riots over the opening of a tunnel in the Old City of Jerusalem were caused by disinformation and appealed for a return to calm.

Speaking to reporters after talks with French President Jacques Chirac, he said the violence might cause a delay of a day or two in talks planned with the Palestinian Authority for Thursday but both sides retained a vital interest in continuing peace negotiations.
Netanyahu said he had not yet been briefed on clashes close to Jerusalem in which Israeli security forces were reported to have shot dead one Palestinian and wounded some 130.
But he said: "I think there have been wild, and unfounded accusations on the tunnel."

"The attempt to portray this as an attack on Arab holy places is totally unfounded, totally incommensurate with the facts and totally incommensurate with our policy of respect for the islamic holy places," he said. "I think there is a combination here of misinformation and deliberate disinformation -- an attempt to whip up passion without any ground of fact."

The hardline Israeli leader said France could act as "an important bridge of understanding" in Arab-Israeli peace negotiations and he had assured Chirac he was committed to moving forward with the Middle East peace process.
